en: Where to Stay: Choose a District Before a Property
zh: 箱根住哪一段：按地区选旅馆
ja: 山のどこに泊まるか：エリアで宿を選ぶ

p.src: A Hakone Town address does not tell you where to stay. Draw one line between the moment you must reach the property tonight and the first place you want to reach tomorrow morning. The map groups lodging into five travel zones: Yumoto and Tonosawa; Miyanoshita and Kowakudani; Gora and Miyagino; Sengokuhara; and Lake Ashi with Ashinoyu. These are decision zones, not administrative borders or hotel rankings. Start with three times: when you can leave today's last stop, when dinner or check-in closes, and where tomorrow's first useful transport begins. Then inspect three pieces of ground: the stop where you get off, the property's actual entrance, and a bad-weather way out. A property that adds a transfer both tonight and tomorrow is not necessarily convenient because it appears central on a map. Choose the part of the mountain first; compare rooms within it second.

caption.zh: 五区图把今晚抵达与明早第一段路连起来。区域不按比例，也不是酒店清单；下车站、真正入口、晚餐与巴士退路都要逐项确认。
caption.ja: 五つの地域で、今夜の到着と翌朝の最初の移動を結ぶ。縮尺図でも宿一覧でもない。降車地点、実際の玄関、夕食、バスの退路を一つずつ確かめる。
caption.en: Five zones connect tonight's arrival to tomorrow's first leg. This is neither a scale map nor a hotel inventory; verify the stop, actual entrance, dinner, and bus fallback separately.

p.src: For a later arrival from Tokyo, or a checkout followed by a direct run to Odawara, Yumoto can remove an extra mountain transfer. The four guides end their sightseeing before dark and use the property confirmation as the day's final route sheet: find the correct station exit, face the right direction outside, then walk, take the stated bus, or wait for a reserved pickup exactly as instructed. Tonosawa lies one stage farther into the railway valley and feels more enclosed than the gateway, but 'a few minutes from the station' says little about moving luggage. A bridge, slope, steps, or a road-side entrance can turn the same map distance into a very different arrival. Yumoto and Tonosawa also belong to Hakone's older onsen landscape. That history explains why long-established properties gather in the valleys; it does not confirm an elevator, bed, or step-free entrance. Stay here because the eastern arrival or departure becomes dependable, not simply because the word traditional sounds appealing.

caption.zh: 把旅馆确认邮件当成当天最后一段交通的终点。按约定时段抵达，登记时一次确认晚餐、浴场、早餐、退房与次日接送。
caption.ja: 宿の予約確認を、その日の移動の終点として使う。指定時刻までに着き、夕食、浴場、朝食、チェックアウト、翌朝の送迎を一度に確かめる。
caption.en: Treat the ryokan confirmation as the endpoint of the day's transport. Arrive within the stated window, then confirm dinner, baths, breakfast, checkout, and next-morning pickup together.

p.src: Miyanoshita and Kowakudani suit a stay built around the mountain railway and museum corridor, but they are not one interchangeable neighbourhood. Ohiradai, Miyanoshita, Kowakudani, Chokoku-no-Mori, and Gora rise in sequence along the line. The train connects them; it does not flatten the slopes between platform, road, and entrance. A stay in Miyanoshita can make its older onsen streets and railway setting part of the evening. From Kowakudani, first identify which station and which side of the road serves tomorrow's museum or bus. When a listing says 'near the museum,' do not stop at the attraction name. Open the walking route, inspect the height change and road, and ask whether it still makes sense with luggage. This corridor is useful not because it is the centre of Hakone, but because today's last stop and tomorrow's first one already follow the same side of the mountain.

p.src: Gora has a clear advantage: the mountain train meets the cable car here, so a morning towards Sounzan, Owakudani, or the upper art route can begin without first retracing the railway. Its cost is equally clear. You have already climbed from Yumoto, the property entrance may continue uphill, and an eastbound departure must descend the mountain again. Do not read 'near Gora Station' as a flat circle. Trace the route from the ticket gates to the door, then verify any evening pickup, last useful service, and luggage storage. Gora and Miyagino share an official area page, but arriving from the railway side is not the same as arriving from the bus side. If tomorrow genuinely begins on the upper route, Gora's higher starting point and interchange reduce backtracking. If tomorrow begins with a direct trip to Odawara, the climb saved tonight has only been moved into the morning.

p.src: Sengokuhara is not a town gathered around one station. It is a broad highland at roughly 650 to 700 metres, with museums, wetland, grassland, and lodging distributed among different bus stops. If a museum or the susuki grassland is the day's main event, staying by the relevant stop can shorten the evening journey back to the property. If you book on the area name alone, the next morning may still begin with a bus in the opposite direction. Find the property's recommended stop, then locate that stop on the current network; do not assume every Sengokuhara address is near Sengoku bus stop. Check whether dinner requires going out, whether the last approach has walking space after dark, and whether a disruption still leaves an exit that does not rely on a fragile chain of connections. Sengokuhara works when the highland itself is given a day. It is not an abstract midpoint on the sightseeing loop.

p.src: 'Lake Ashi side' is not one stop either. Togendai at the north end joins ropeway, boat, and bus. Moto-Hakone and Hakone-machi on the south shore have different port and bus relationships; Hakone-en has another approach; Ashinoyu sits above the shore. Choose the side from the place you will actually see in the morning. The shrine and cedar avenue, the checkpoint and Onshi Park, and Togendai with Owakudani do not share one starting point. A lake or Fuji view is a weather-given extra, not a substitute for transport that runs. Before booking, save a bus exit that does not depend on the boat or ropeway and verify the last useful service. A quiet cove also has a practical cost if dinner is not included and the nearest shop requires a long walk. Stay by the lake to give the shore an evening and a morning, not merely to add 'lake view' to the room name.

p.src: The four guides divide the checks that determine whether one night will work. In a representative room, Aya-chan checks bed height and night lighting; Lala Xia checks the entrance threshold and space to open luggage; Sasa-kun locates the in-room toilet and shower; and the Zhuangzi robot records the answers about meals, baths, and pickup in the booking notes. This is not a bookable hotel room or a claim of accessibility. It separates features that listing pages often blur together. Before paying, confirm the selected date and room: futon or bed; toilet and shower inside or outside the room; steps from lift or stairs to the door; private bath in-room or reserved by time; whether that bath is labelled as onsen; dinner and breakfast inclusion and location; dietary response; tattoo policy; latest arrival; and checkout. When any answer determines whether the stay is usable, obtain it in writing instead of filling the gap with what a ryokan usually provides.

caption.zh: 这间示意客房把门槛、床高、行李空间、座椅与卫浴路线分开呈现。它不是可预订房间，也不表示无障碍；订房时要逐项向旅馆确认。
caption.ja: 説明用の客室で、段差、ベッド高、荷物空間、椅子、水回りへの経路を分けて見る。予約できる部屋でもバリアフリーの表示でもないため、各条件は宿へ確認する。
caption.en: This representative room separates the threshold, bed height, luggage space, chair, and bathroom route. It is neither bookable inventory nor an accessibility claim; confirm each condition with the property.

p.src: Luggage delivery moves the luggage, not the traveller. Hakone's current service works in both directions between Hakone-Yumoto Station and participating properties, but direction, cutoff, dimensions, weight, excluded items, payment, collection window, and weather conditions must be checked on the current page. Find the selected property on the partner list before planning to send the large bag. If it is absent, arrange storage or carry the bag yourself. A listing that says shuttle still needs four answers: how to reserve, where it collects, when it runs, and whom to contact when delayed. Then write down the single most fragile leg: a slope after the last bus, a lake connection lost to suspension, steps with a suitcase in rain, or a tight transfer before dinner closes. If you can explain that leg before booking, arrival day no longer depends on luck.

p.src: Begin with the Hakone Tourist Association directory, narrowing by area and accommodation type, then use only the filters that matter: beds, wheelchair rooms, private baths, shuttle, children, pets, or other stated needs. A result is a shortlist, not proof that the selected room has the feature on your dates. Keep three to five candidates, open each official property and room page, and send the same short enquiry to those that remain. State dates, party size, and room name; ask for the actual entrance and stop, final pickup, bedding and bathroom, steps, meals and dietary response, bath and tattoo policy, latest arrival, cancellation terms, and all required charges. Compare whether the whole night works and what the whole route costs, not one headline room rate. When an answer is vague, ask until it supports a decision or remove the property.

p.src: Use four trip shapes to test the district. Evening arrival from Tokyo followed by departure next day: protect arrival in Yumoto or Tonosawa. Railway and art today, Sounzan tomorrow: choose Miyanoshita, Kowakudani, or Gora by the stop that removes backtracking. Museums and grassland for a full day: stay in Sengokuhara near the right bus stop. Shrine, cedars, checkpoint, or Togendai to Owakudani tomorrow: use the matching lake shore and retain a bus exit. Between two otherwise similar properties, choose the one that you can reach before dinner, that you can leave in poor weather, and that gives you the shorter first leg next morning.
